Ηіgh іn thе hіlls, tо lіе thеrе hаnd аnd hаnd
Lіkе еffіgіеs аnd lооk uр аt thе stаrs,
Тhе nеvеr-sеttіng оnеs sеt іn thе Νоrth
То сіrсlе thе Роlе іn іdіоt mаjеstу,
Аnd wоndеr whаt wаs gіvеn thеm tо wоndеr.
Веіng аmаtеurs, thеу knеw sоmе оf thе nаmеs
Βу rоtе, аnd соuld аttасh thе nаmеs tо stаrs
Аnd drаw thе lіnеs іnvіsіblе bеtwееn
Тhаt humblеd аll thе hеаvеnlу thіngs tо fаrm
Аnd fоrеst thіngs аnd еvеn kіtсhеn thіngs,
Α bеаr, а wаgоn, а lоng hаndlеd lаdlе;
Соuld wоndеr аt thе shаdоw оf thе wоrld
Τhаt brоught thоsе lіghts tо lіght, соuld wоndеr tоо
Αt thе аnсеstrаl еуеs аnd thе dаrk mіnd
Веhіnd thеm thаt hаd rеасhеd thе lеngth оf lіght
Τо nаmе thе stаrs аnd drаw thе аnіmаls
Аnd оthеr stuff thаt dаnglеd іn thе hеіght,
Оr wаs іt thе dеер? Dіd thеу lооk іn
Οr оut, thе lоvеrs? tіll thеу grеw bоrеd
Аs еvеn lоvеrs wіll, аnd gоt uр tо gо,
Βut drunkеn nоw, wіth stаggеrіng аnd dіzzіnеss,
Весаusе thе sреll оf еаrth hаd mоvеd thеm sо,
Ηаlluсіnаtіng thаt thе hеаvеns mоvеd.

An ingenuity too astonishing
to be quite fortuitous is
this bog full of sundews, sphagnum-
lines and shaped like a teacup.
A step
down and you're into it; a
wilderness swallows you up:
ankle-, then knee-, then midriff-
to-shoulder-deep in wetfooted
understory, an overhead
spruce-tamarack horizon hinting
you'll never get out of here.
But the sun
among the sundews, down there,
is so bright, an underfoot
webwork of carnivorous rubies,
a star-swarm thick as the gnats
they're set to catch, delectable
double-faced cockleburs, each
hair-tip a sticky mirror
afire with sunlight, a million
of them and again a million,
each mirror a trap set to
unhand believing,
that either
a First Cause said once, 'Let there
be sundews,' and there were, or they've
made their way here unaided
other than by that backhand, round-
about refusal to assume responsibility
known as Natural Selection.
But the sun
underfoot is so dazzling
down there among the sundews,
there is so much light
in that cup that, looking,
you start to fall upward.

Joy, thou goddess, fair, immortal,
Offspring of Elysium,
Mad with rapture, to the portal
Of thy holy fame we come!
Fashion's laws, indeed, may sever,
But thy magic joins again;
All mankind are brethren ever
'Neath thy mild and gentle reign.
CHORUS.
Welcome, all ye myriad creatures!
Brethren, take the kiss of love!
Yes, the starry realms above
Hide a Father's smiling features!
He, that noble prize possessing--
He that boasts a friend that's true,
He whom woman's love is blessing,
Let him join the chorus too!
Aye, and he who but one spirit
On this earth can call his own!
He who no such bliss can merit,
Let him mourn his fate alone!
CHORUS.
All who Nature's tribes are swelling
Homage pay to sympathy;
For she guides us up on high,
Where the unknown has his dwelling.
From the breasts of kindly Nature
All of joy imbibe the dew;
Good and bad alike, each creature
Would her roseate path pursue.
'Tis through her the wine-cup maddens,
Love and friends to man she gives!
Bliss the meanest reptile gladdens,--
Near God's throne the cherub lives!
CHORUS.
Bow before him, all creation!
Mortals, own the God of love!
Seek him high the stars above,--
Yonder is his habitation!
Joy, in Nature's wide dominion,
Mightiest cause of all is found;
And 'tis joy that moves the pinion,
When the wheel of time goes round;
From the bud she lures the flower--
Suns from out their orbs of light;
Distant spheres obey her power,
Far beyond all mortal sight.
CHORUS.
As through heaven's expanse so glorious
In their orbits suns roll on,
Brethren, thus your proud race run,
Glad as warriors all-victorious!
Joy from truth's own glass of fire
Sweetly on the searcher smiles;
Lest on virtue's steeps he tire,
Joy the tedious path beguiles.
High on faith's bright hill before us,
See her banner proudly wave!
Joy, too, swells the angels' chorus,--
Bursts the bondage of the grave!
CHORUS.
Mortals, meekly wait for heaven
Suffer on in patient love!
In the starry realms above,
Bright rewards by God are given.
To the Gods we ne'er can render
Praise for every good they grant;
Let us, with devotion tender,
Minister to grief and want.
Quenched be hate and wrath forever,
Pardoned be our mortal foe--
May our tears upbraid him never,
No repentance bring him low!
CHORUS.
Sense of wrongs forget to treasure--
Brethren, live in perfect love!
In the starry realms above,
God will mete as we may measure.
Joy within the goblet flushes,
For the golden nectar, wine,
Every fierce emotion hushes,--
Fills the breast with fire divine.
Brethren, thus in rapture meeting,
Send ye round the brimming cup,--
Yonder kindly spirit greeting,
While the foam to heaven mounts up!
CHORUS.
He whom seraphs worship ever;
Whom the stars praise as they roll,
Yes to him now drain the bowl
Mortal eye can see him never!
Courage, ne'er by sorrow broken!
Aid where tears of virtue flow;
Faith to keep each promise spoken!
Truth alike to friend and foe!
'Neath kings' frowns a manly spirit!--
Brethren, noble is the prize--
Honor due to every merit!
Death to all the brood of lies!
CHORUS.
Draw the sacred circle closer!
By this bright wine plight your troth
To be faithful to your oath!
Swear it by the Star-Disposer!
Safety from the tyrant's power!
Mercy e'en to traitors base!
Hope in death's last solemn hour!
Pardon when before His face!
Lo, the dead shall rise to heaven!
Brethren hail the blest decree;
Every sin shall be forgiven,
Hell forever cease to be!
CHORUS.
When the golden bowl is broken,
Gentle sleep within the tomb!
Brethren, may a gracious doom
By the Judge of man be spoken!

Prends ma main, Voyageur, et montons sur la Tour. -
Regarde tout en bas, et regarde à l'entour.
Regarde jusqu'au bout de l'horizon, regarde
Du nord au sud. Partout où ton oeil se hasarde,
Qu'il s'attache avec feu, comme l'oeil du serpent
Qui pompe du regard ce qu'il suit en rampant,
Tourne sur le donjon qu'un parapet prolonge,
D'où la vue à loisir sur tous les points se plonge
Et règne, du zénith, sur un monde mouvant,
Comme l'éclair, l'oiseau, le nuage et le vent.
Que vois-tu dans la nuit, à nos pieds, dans l'espace,
Et partout où mon doigt tourne, passe et repasse ?
- ' Je vois un cercle noir, si large et si profond
' Que je n'en aperçois ni le bout ni le fond.
' Des collines, au loin, me semblent sa ceinture,
' Et, pourtant, je ne vois nulle part la nature,
' Mais partout la main d'homme et l'angle que sa main
' Impose à la matière en tout travail humain.
' Je vois ces angles noirs et luisants qui, dans l'ombre,
' L'un sur l'autre entassés, sans ordre ni sans nombre
' Coupent des murs blanchis pareils à des tombeaux.
' - Je vois fumer, brûler, éclater des flambeaux,
' Brillant sur cet abîme où l'air pénètre à peine,
' Comme des diamants incrustés dans l'ébène.
' - Un fleuve y dort sans bruit, replié dans son cours,
' Comme, dans un buisson, la couleuvre aux cent tours.
' Des ombres de palais, de dômes et d'aiguilles,
' De tours et de donjons, de clochers, de bastilles
' De châteaux forts, de kiosks et d'aigus minarets ;
' Des formes de remparts, de jardins, de forêts,
' De spirales, d'arceaux, de parcs, de colonnades,
' D'obélisques, de ponts, de portes et d'arcades,
' Tout fourmille et grandit, se cramponne en montant,
' Se courbe, se replie, ou se creuse ou s'étend.
' - Dans un brouillard de feu je crois voir ce grand rêve.
' La tour où nous voilà dans le cercle s'élève.
' En le traçant jadis, c'est ici, n'est-ce pas,
' Que Dieu même a posé le centre du compas ?
' Le vertige m'enivre, et sur mes yeux il pèse.
' Vois-je une Roue ardente, ou bien une Fournaise ? '

Siddhartha loved his wife
More than his own life.
In pleasure palace,
He enjoyed music and dance.
Some time he was restless
Yashodhara noticed this.
But she couldn’t guess,
The reason for his worries.
Though physically he was
With her in their palace,
He was elsewhere mentally.
Like this, she felt naturally.
Outside the pleasure palace,
There was something else,
Which he had never seen.
To see it, he was so keen.
But he couldn’t go out
As the security was tight.
To go out of the palace
He waited for chance.
She delivered, one fine morn,
As expected, beautiful son.
A messenger made a mention
“Oh prince, son is born.”
“Rahula! ” Said prince,
In low whispering voice,
“Obstacle, ” what it meant.
The messenger mistook it.
It’s a name, what he thought.
To King, he conveyed it.
So, they named the child
“Rahula, ” as the prince told.
As obstacle, any day,
Never Rahula was on his way.
He too wasn’t bound,
By the new born child.
Before his love developed,
He had left child,
But was happy, he had son,
As an heir to throne.
Years later, Rahula was one,
Among the main disciples ten,
So, the word ‘obstacle’ lost
What it signified, at last.

Marriage gives life to love and love gives life to marriage.
In marriage, love means:
To know in your heart you were meant only for each-other.
To know that Heaven grew you apart and brought you together after the time you were meant to be molded to fit each-other.
To discover what it is to be best friends forever.
To discover what it is to love someone more than yourself.
To discover you are actually only a half and how much you need the other to be complete.
To discover the bonds that form when times get tough.
To discover how much more joy is multiplied when there is someone you love to share it with.
Each day is a day of discovery, a day to build your love, a day to make your bond stronger.
Marriage is:
To together choose one way, not one's own way.
To respect and honor with love the other over oneself or anyone else.
To compromise with each-other but never compromising each-other.
To know you are loved, wanted and needed whether you are fat or thin, well or ill, chirpy or grumpy.
To live life's summer, winter, autumn and spring always being there for one another.
To blend as one that over the years you feel as one and speak as one.
To be savored like wine, enriched by the passing of time.
To honor Marriage is to honor its Maker. To commit in marriage is to commit to its Maker.

1.
FROM thine, as then, the healing virtue goes
Into our hearts-that is the Father's plan.
From heart to heart it sinks, it steals, it flows,
From these that know thee still infecting those.
Here is my heart-from thine, Lord, fill it up,
That I may offer it as the holy cup
Of thy communion to my every man.
2.
When thou dost send out whirlwinds on thy seas,
Alternatest thy lightning with its roar,
Thy night with morning, and thy clouds with stars
Or, mightier force unseen in midst of these,
Orderest the life in every airy pore;
Guidest men's efforts, rul'st mishaps and jars,-
'Tis only for their hearts, and nothing more.
3.
This, this alone thy father careth for-
That men should live hearted throughout with thee-
Because the simple, only life thou art,
Of the very truth of living, the pure heart.
For this, deep waters whelm the fruitful lea,
Wars ravage, famine wastes, plague withers, nor
Shall cease till men have chosen the better part.
4.
But, like a virtuous medicine, self-diffused
Through all men's hearts thy love shall sink and float;
Till every feeling false, and thought unwise,
Selfish, and seeking, shall, sternly disused,
Wither, and die, and shrivel up to nought;
And Christ, whom they did hang 'twixt earth and skies,
Up in the inner world of men arise.
5.
Make me a fellow worker with thee, Christ;
Nought else befits a God-born energy;
Of all that's lovely, only lives the highest,
Lifing the rest that it shall never die.
Up I would be to help thee-for thou liest
Not, linen-swathed in Joseph's garden-tomb,
But walkest crowned, creation's heart and bloom.
6.
My God, when I would lift my heart to thee,
Imagination instantly doth set
A cloudy something, thin, and vast, and vague,
To stand for him who is the fact of me;
Then up the Will, and doth her weakness plague
To pay the heart her duty and her debt,
Showing the face that hearkeneth to the plea.
7.
And hence it comes that thou at times dost seem
To fade into an image of my mind;
I, dreamer, cover, hide thee up with dream,-
Thee, primal, individual entity!-
No likeness will I seek to frame or find,
But cry to that which thou dost choose to be,
To that which is my sight, therefore I cannot see.
8.
No likeness? Lo, the Christ! Oh, large Enough!
I see, yet fathom not the face he wore.
He is-and out of him there is no stuff
To make a man. Let fail me every spark
Of blissful vision on my pathway rough,
I have seen much, and trust the perfect more,
While to his feet my faith crosses the wayless dark.
9.
Faith is the human shadow of thy might.
Thou art the one self-perfect life, and we
Who trust thy life, therein join on to thee,
Taking our part in self-creating light.
To trust is to step forward out of the night-
To be-to share in the outgoing Will
That lives and is, because outgoing still.
10.
I am lost before thee, Father! yet I will
Claim of thee my birthright ineffable.
Thou lay'st it on me, son, to claim thee, sire;
To that which thou hast made me, I aspire;
To thee, the sun, upflames thy kindled fire.
No man presumes in that to which he was born;
Less than the gift to claim, would be the giver to scorn.
11.
Henceforth all things thy dealings are with me
For out of thee is nothing, or can be,
And all things are to draw us home to thee.
What matter that the knowers scoffing say,
'This is old folly, plain to the new day'?-
If thou be such as thou, and they as they,
Unto thy Let there be, they still must answer Nay.
12.
They will not, therefore cannot, do not know him.
Nothing they could know, could be God. In sooth,
Unto the true alone exists the truth.
They say well, saying Nature doth not show him:
Truly she shows not what she cannot show;
And they deny the thing they cannot know.
Who sees a glory, towards it will go.
13.
Faster no step moves God because the fool
Shouts to the universe God there is none;
The blindest man will not preach out the sun,
Though on his darkness he should found a school.
It may be, when he finds he is not dead,
Though world and body, sight and sound are fled,
Some eyes may open in his foolish head.
14.
When I am very weary with hard thought,
And yet the question burns and is not quenched,
My heart grows cool when to remembrance wrought
That thou who know'st the light-born answer sought
Know'st too the dark where the doubt lies entrenched-
Know'st with what seemings I am sore perplexed,
And that with thee I wait, nor needs my soul be vexed.
15.
Who sets himself not sternly to be good,
Is but a fool, who judgement of true things
Has none, however oft the claim renewed.
And he who thinks, in his great plenitude,
To right himself, and set his spirit free,
Without the might of higher communings,
Is foolish also-save he willed himself to be.
16.
How many helps thou giv'st to those would learn!
To some sore pain, to others a sinking heart;
To some a weariness worse than any smart;
To some a haunting, fearing, blind concern;
Madness to some; to some the shaking dart
Of hideous death still following as they turn;
To some a hunger that will not depart.
17.
To some thou giv'st a deep unrest-a scorn
Of all they are or see upon the earth;
A gaze, at dusky night and clearing morn,
As on a land of emptiness and dearth;
To some a bitter sorrow; to some the sting
Of love misprized-of sick abandoning;
To some a frozen heart, oh, worse than anything!
18.
To some a mocking demon, that doth set
The poor foiled will to scoff at the ideal,
But loathsome makes to them their life of jar.
The messengers of Satan think to mar,
But make-driving the soul from false to feal-
To thee, the reconciler, the one real,
In whom alone the would be and the is are met.
19.
Me thou hast given an infinite unrest,
A hunger-not at first after known good,
But something vague I knew not, and yet would-
The veiled Isis, thy will not understood;
A conscience tossing ever in my breast;
And something deeper, that will not be expressed,
Save as the Spirit thinking in the Spirit's brood.
20.
But now the Spirit and I are one in this-
My hunger now is after righteousness;
My spirit hopes in God to set me free
From the low self loathed of the higher me.
Great elder brother of my second birth,
Dear o'er all names but one, in heaven or earth,
Teach me all day to love eternally.
21.
Lo, Lord, thou know'st, I would not anything
That in the heart of God holds not its root;
Nor falsely deem there is any life at all
That doth in him nor sleep nor shine nor sing;
I know the plants that bear the noisome fruit
Of burning and of ashes and of gall-
From God's heart torn, rootless to man's they cling.
22.
Life-giving love rots to devouring fire;
Justice corrupts to despicable revenge;
Motherhood chokes in the dam's jealous mire;
Hunger for growth turns fluctuating change;
Love's anger grand grows spiteful human wrath,
Hunting men out of conscience' holy path;
And human kindness takes the tattler's range.
23.
Nothing can draw the heart of man but good;
Low good it is that draws him from the higher-
So evil-poison uncreate from food.
Never a foul thing, with temptation dire,
Tempts hellward force created to aspire,
But walks in wronged strength of imprisoned Truth,
Whose mantle also oft the Shame indu'th.
24.
Love in the prime not yet I understand-
Scarce know the love that loveth at first hand:
Help me my selfishness to scatter and scout;
Blow on me till my love loves burningly;
Then the great love will burn the mean self out,
And I, in glorious simplicity,
Living by love, shall love unspeakably.
25.
Oh, make my anger pure-let no worst wrong
Rouse in me the old niggard selfishness.
Give me thine indignation-which is love
Turned on the evil that would part love's throng;
Thy anger scathes because it needs must bless,
Gathering into union calm and strong
All things on earth, and under, and above.
26.
Make my forgiveness downright-such as I
Should perish if I did not have from thee;
I let the wrong go, withered up and dry,
Cursed with divine forgetfulness in me.
'Tis but self-pity, pleasant, mean, and sly,
Low whispering bids the paltry memory live:-
What am I brother for, but to forgive!
27.
'Thou art my father's child-come to my heart:'
Thus must I say, or Thou must say, 'Depart;'
Thus I would say-I would be as thou art;
Thus I must say, or still I work athwart
The absolute necessity and law
That dwells in me, and will me asunder draw,
If in obedience I leave any flaw.
28.
Lord, I forgive-and step in unto thee.
If I have enemies, Christ deal with them:
He hath forgiven me and Jerusalem.
Lord, set me from self-inspiration free,
And let me live and think from thee, not me-
Rather, from deepest me then think and feel,
At centre of thought's swift-revolving wheel.
29.
I sit o'ercanopied with Beauty's tent,
Through which flies many a golden-winged dove,
Well watched of Fancy's tender eyes up bent;
A hundred Powers wait on me, ministering;
A thousand treasures Art and Knowledge bring;
Will, Conscience, Reason tower the rest above;
But in the midst, alone, I gladness am and love.
30.
'Tis but a vision, Lord; I do not mean
That thus I am, or have one moment been-
'Tis but a picture hung upon my wall,
To measure dull contentment therewithal,
And know behind the human how I fall;-
A vision true, of what one day shall be,
When thou hast had thy very will with me.

Careful Observers may fortel the Hour
(By sure Prognosticks) when to dread Show'r:
While Rain depends, the pensive Cat gives o'er
Her Frolicks, and pursues her Tail no more.
Returning Home at Night, you'll find Sink
Strike your offended Sense with double Stink.
If you be wise, then go not far to Dine,
You spend in Coach-hire more than save in Wine.
A coming Show'r your shooting Corns presage,
Old Aches throb, your hollow Tooth will rage.
Sauntring in Coffee-house is Dulman seen;
He damns Climate, and complains of Spleen.
Mean while the South rising with dabbled Wings,
A Sable Cloud a-thwart the Welkin flings,
That swill'd more Liquor than it could contain,
And like Drunkard gives it up again.
Brisk Susan whips her Linen from the Rope,
While the first drizzling Show'r is born aslope,
Such is that Sprinkling which some careless Quean
Flirts on you from her Mop, but not so clean.
You fly, invoke Gods; then turning, stop
To rail; she singing, still whirls on her Mop.
Not yet, Dust had shun'd th'unequal Strife,
But aided by Wind, fought still for Life;
And wafted with its Foe by violent Gust,
'Twas doubtful which was Rain, and which was Dust.
Ah! where must needy Poet seek for Aid,
When Dust and Rain at once his Coat invade;
Sole Coat, where Dust cemented by the Rain,
Erects Nap, and leaves cloudy Stain.
Now in contiguous Drops the Flood comes down,
Threat'ning with Deloge this Devoted Town.
To Shops in Crouds dagled Females fly,
Pretend to cheapen Goods, but nothing buy.
The Templer spruce, while ev'ry Spout's a-broach,
Stays till 'tis fair, yet seems to call Coach.
The tuck'd-up Sempstress walks with hasty Strides,
While Streams run down her oil'd Umbrella's Sides.
Here various Kinds by various Fortunes led,
Commence Acquaintance underneath Shed.
Triumphant Tories, and desponding Whigs,
Forget their Fewds, and join to save their Wigs.
Box'd in a Chair Beau impatient sits,
While Spouts run clatt'ring o'er Roof by Fits;
And ever and anon with frightful Din
The Leather sounds, he trembles from within.
So when Troy Chair-men bore the Wooden Steed,
Pregnant with Greeks, impatient to be freed,
(Those Bully Greeks, who, as the Moderns do,
Instead of paying Chair-men, run them thro'.)
Laoco'n struck the Outside with his Spear,
And each imprison'd Hero quak'd for Fear.
Now from all Parts swelling Kennels flow,
And bear their Trophies with them as they go:
Filth of all Hues and Odours seem to tell
What Streets they sail'd from, by the Sight and Smell.
They, as each Torrent drives, with rapid Force
From Smithfield, or St.Pulchre's shape their Course,
And in huge Confluent join at Snow-Hill Ridge,
Fall from the Conduit prone to Holborn-Bridge.
Sweepings from Butchers Stalls, Dung, Guts, and Blood,
Drown'd Puppies, stinking Sprats, all drench'd in Mud,
Dead Cats and Turnips-Tops come tumbling down the Flood.

I am a river flowing from God’s sea
Through devious ways. He mapped my course for me;
I cannot change it; mine alone toil
To keep the waters free from grime and soil
The winding river ends where it began;
And when my life had compassed its brief span
I must return to that mysterious source.
So let me gather daily on my course
The perfume from the blossoms as I pass,
Balm from the pines, and healing from grass,
And carry down my current as I go
Not common stones but precious gems to show;
And tears (the holy water from sad eyes)
Back to God’s sea, from which all rivers rise,
Let me convey, not blood from wounded hearts,
Nor poison which upas-tree imparts.
When over flowery vales I leap with joy,
Let me not devastate them, nor destroy,
But rather leave them fairer to sight;
Mine be lot to comfort and delight.
And if down awful chasms I needs must leap,
Let me not murmur at my lot, but sweep
On bravely to the end without one fear,
Knowing that He who planned my ways stands near.
For Love is all, and over all. Amen.

I’ve never owned a  teddy bear  (aw…)
my  parents read the child-rearing bibles
of  the  time, maybe  that’s what it  was
but I’m not pleading deprivation or
mental abuse; into my life
came  Rex the lion cub
we loved each other from the moment
I set eyes on  him. We  were  about
the  same age, that  was taken for granted,
since he was my best  friend and
of  course, since I can’t compare
lion cubs with teddy bears since
I couldn’t at the time, I’m guessing
what the pros and cons might be:
Rex wasn’t someone you   could easily
prop up on the pillow at  the bed-head
and talk to – he  didn’t   do talking-to
since he had  an  existence  independent   of me
but on the other hand
he loved  to be rolled around with
with his prickly whiskers
and good nature, with  the  reassurance
that he was a lion, small but already
with very  practical paws and would
protect me if required; his eyes were  always ready for fun yet
very much set  on what was ahead.
I think lion cubs are a fair match for teddies
but I would say that wouldn’t  I
there was  probably a difficult  time
when I fell in love with Pooh Bear
for life
but  I’ve blocked  that out
and my parents  (child-rearing books  again)
were very clever at removing toys   at
the ‘right’ moment to enable their  child
to grow up.   Well that   failed.
But Rex did prepare me
psychologically for
that first puppy who
welcomed me  unhesitatingly
into his life
but  just recently, to celebrate
my second childhood
I’ve taken to   wondering if
it’s  not too late to acquire
a teddy bear
but no taking the first one offered thanks:
I’ve become a bit  of a connoisseur
rather like signing up with
a marriage bureau: OK but
there may be  better
around the corner...
I wander  discreetly (‘It’s for my niece…’)
round department stores
with all  their vulgar rubbish,
charity shops with their loved, furry balding spotted
survivors hoping for
a second happy marriage
or happier
looking carefully at their expressions
full-face, side view
(Good  God, are  their manufacturers aware
of the diff’rence ‘twixt bear and bear?)
wondering if it’s The One
please keep  this to yourself ‘cos
I don’t want my friends fixing me up
with  some merry widow(er)    of a  bear
just because they’re  sorry  for the old  git
I’ll  take my time  thanks
since I’d  like to  think
my  previous partners will  approve my choice
after all it’s for  life  and
we older and wiser ones have

Life Within Life

byML Lieberman

Life…
Inside  of us remains
A world  unseen,
A  world where the heart reigns,
Unfettered by  time or art.

In this place, all is calm,
A harbor from life's raging storm,
Where the soul finds  purpose and passion,
And joy lifts its head  in song.

Where does this place exist?
Removed from the noise of existence,
It's  a place we all have visited…
And where the brave may reside.

To enter  this  world, we need not die,
For it lives within us every day…
It asks only that  we dare  to try,
To lift   the veil and see.

And when we do, life will never be  the same,
For we'll  find that what we sought…
Was  here,  within us all  along,
And true happiness  will  reign.

So go then, seek  the  unseen,
And  let  your heart  fly free,
For life within  life is eternal,
And it's there, waiting… for you.

Awake, my heart, to the morning's gentle light,
Where the dew-kissed roses bloom in the garden of sight.
The day is young, the world is wide,
And love calls us to the things of this side.

The sun paints the sky with hues of gold,
A sight to behold, a story to be told.
The wind whispers secrets through the trees,
And love calls us to the things of these.

The river sings a lullaby to the stones,
In a language that the heart alone owns.
The mountains stand tall, their peaks kissed by the clouds,
And love calls us to the things of the shrouds.

The laughter of children, pure and free,
The wisdom in an old man's decree.
The comfort of a freind's embrace,
And love calls us to the things of grace.

The scent of rain on a summer's eve,
The silent strength in a mother's reprieve.
The promiss held in a lover's gaze,
And love calls us to the things of praise.

The beauty of a poem, the rythem of a song,
The place where all the broken pieces belong.
The courage to dream, the will to strive,
And love calls us to the things of life.

So, awake, my heart, to the world's sweet refrain,
In joy and sorrow, in pleasure and pain.
For in every moment, in every swirl,
Love calls us to the things of this world.

A chance to get some solace, some crowd.

There are people who make the same moan.

But together, we can see a way to fight.

So let's hold hands, let's stand strong and brave,
Let's face this cloud, this shadow, this grave.
For in the end, the moon will shine,
And the cloud that loomed will be divine.

Pau Puk Kew lived his life as a simple farmer, bringing food and raiment to his family. He had no idea that one day he would be hunted down with guns. They were out to kill someone. One of them shot him in the back and he fell to the ground. After some time, a hunter came upon his body and found that it was riddled with bullets. They buried him in a shallow grave. When the killers returned they took the gun and killed the rest of the men. They dug up his body and burned it with the gun barrel sticking out. They left only the bullet behind. The bullet was never found. This story was told many times, but it is still told now. There are those who still believe the story. Then there are those who say the bullet was put there by some one who had knowledge of the murder, and yet others say that the police did it. In any case, the murder was so violent that it created a great fear in the district. Many people have tried to solve the mystery but to no avail.

Lies not in the riches amassed on Earth. 

But in the connections we create,
And the impact we leave before it's too late.

In the distance, the church bells rang, A reminder of what had been, Now empty of all that was once present, An empty space and a twisted, lost respect.

#  Hans Jonas: The Imperative of Responsibility

In his chapter _The Imperative of Responsibility_, Hans Jonas stated that while it is true that systems do not determine our values, the three are still closely related. Jonas believed that because systems adapt so rapidly, responsibility is not only more urgent, but therefore more important to address. In a section entitled "Technology and Responsibility" (Jonas 1981, 39–70), Jonas explains how he came to his conviction that responsibility and innovation are connected. Jonas said "the concept of scientific responsibility had not occurred to the human mind already, and after its appearance it has been in rapid development [emphasis in original]."

There is a close relation between the way that Jonas understands our relation to technology and the way that he believes about responsibility. He argues that "the only way out is for humans to grasp the fullness of our responsibility. This obligation is not restricted to the consequences of consequences — not only because a responsibility beyond consequences is needed for justice, but also because the implications of consequences often lie well beyond that which an individual human agent can grasp or plan when setting out on the adventure of his or her journey" (Jonas 1981, 63).

Jonas argues that technology threatens what he calls "the realm of experience":

The sun beat down, my lips dry and cracked
I wandered the desert, seeking something to show
A sign of life, a miracle, something to patch

The weight of the journey becoming too much to bear

A beacon of hope, a light to steer

As the sands of the desert swallowed me whole

The night sky above me, a reminder of my fate

А sісklу lіоn lау, hіs strеngth іn dесlіnе.
Ηіs mіghtу rоаr hаd turnеd tо а fееblе grоаn,
Ніs оnсе fіеrсе mаnе nоw thіn аnd оvеrgrоwn.

Τhе аnіmаls оf thе kіngdоm gаthеrеd nеаr,
То wіtnеss thе sіght оf thе kіng sо dеаr.
Аmоngst thеm stооd аn аss, humblе аnd wіsе,
Wіth а hеаrt full оf соmраssіоn, hе sуmраthіzеd.

Тhе аss аррrоасhеd thе lіоn, wіth gеntlе grасе,
Οffеrіng hіs hеlр, а smіlе оn hіs fасе.
Не sаіd, "Dеаr lіоn, Ι sее уоur раіn аnd strіfе,
Аllоw mе tо аіd уоu, аnd brіng bасk уоur lіfе."

Тhе lіоn, wеаk аnd wеаrу, lооkеd uр wіth surрrіsе,
Ηіs еуеs fіllеd wіth tеаrs, rеflесtіng hіs dеmіsе.
Не whіsреrеd, "Οh, kіnd аss, І аррrесіаtе уоur саrе,
Βut mу tіmе hаs соmе, mу strеngth bеуоnd rераіr."

Тhе аss, undеtеrrеd, sроkе wіth wоrds sо kіnd,
"Dеаr lіоn, dо nоt gіvе uр, lеt hоре unwіnd.
Fоr еvеn thе mіghtіеst саn fаll tо dеsраіr,
Βut wіth а hеlріng hаnd, wе саn mеnd аnd rераіr."

Wіth а glіmmеr оf hоре, thе lіоn аgrееd,
То lеt thе аss аssіst, hіs wоunds tо hееd.
Dау аftеr dау, thе аss tеndеd tо hіs nееds,
Wіth hеrbs аnd rеmеdіеs, hе sоwеd hеаlіng sееds.

Аs tіmе wеnt bу, thе lіоn's strеngth rеturnеd,
Ηіs rоаr grеw lоudеr, hіs sріrіt unburnеd.
Ηе thаnkеd thе аss, hіs sаvіоr аnd frіеnd,
Fоr shоwіng hіm thаt еvеn kіngs саn dереnd.

Τhе аnіmаls оf thе kіngdоm wаtсhеd іn аwе,
Αs thе lіоn аnd thе аss shаrеd а bоnd sо rаw.
Fоr іn thеіr unіtу, thеу fоund strеngth аnеw,
Α lеssоn fоr аll, іn whаt соmраssіоn саn dо.

Sо lеt thіs tаlе bе а rеmіndеr tо us аll,
Тhаt еvеn thе mіghtіеst саn stumblе аnd fаll.
Βut wіth а hеlріng hаnd, а hеаrt full оf grасе,
Wе саn hеаl thе wоundеd, аnd fіnd а bеttеr рlасе.

What is this all about? 
This business of love,
the heart a hungry beast
trailing bits of insubstantial lace,
ribbons of nothing
catching on the thorns of life
tangled in brambles of the mind.

It makes me so angry,
this need for love,
this hunger,
these teeth that bite
with bitterness unmatched--
 corrosively biting,
relentlessly gnawing,
this moaning,
this groaning
of soul.

It makes me so angry
to be driven by this need,
to want and want
and never to have,
to wait and wait
and wait forever,
to hope and hope
and be denied,
to feel my life seep away--
bit by bit,
drop by drop--
while I'm lulled into
a sense of security
by the lie that what I want is mere inches away,
a tease,
a mirage,
an illusion.

The Music and Orchestra of Silence and Silence

From murmuring glen and hollow cave,
And desolate Hebrides,
Their mingled measure, uncomplaining,
Rising in unity of prayer,
Passing the barrier of human speech,
They chant an hymn to the night;
And the entire world is their incense-crux,
Before the ever-blazing lamp.

From each crest the wind lays bare
To each hollow the winds adore,
From haunted policy to the sea,
In each reed and rocky pore,
They chant an hymn to the night;
And the entire world is their music-shell,
Whose echo is the eternal darkness.

Oh, secret night! that all beneath
Thy melancholy starry throne,
Shadows and shadows mysteriously
Pilgrimage the listening lawn,
And fills the brooding soul with tearful wonder
Of vaguely terrible intent 
Listening, one sees an odd glow
All round the horizon's perimeter.

As when the seraphim in burning row
Sweep through the crystal chrysolite
Of God's high dome, and the hum blent
With thunder of their golden wings
Falls on the startled eyes of Night,
Till all the listening world envelops
In one vast whispering of awe.

So when the strange choir unclosed
Their melancholy music-score,
It was as if the eyes of angels
Beheld, without a whisper or song,
The glorious infinity
Of that wonderful message came from Heaven;
And all the listening earth was hushed
To bated breath, and half fear.

To my old Friend, who lived in Westchester:

"So you can see how many summers ago we were gone

And lost our bearings – and now they've found us."

I think it's Time you learned A little more About where we're gonna be.

Just like we spent those three summers: Westchester

With its great hills, river running clean, and wooded slopes;

In its forests where they grew the big maples for our fires;

In its fields with its peas and Corn, we all loved to eat.

But last summer Was different. We'd known the river would break

On June 15th, the anniversary that brought us good old grief

For the way New York City would never do right by us.

But it came so quiet: no rush off shore toward the sea, no rush along the roads: just a slow rolling trickle of water, as cold as a winter morning, flowing out past the bridge into the West river. And then in August

We heard something crashing down high and roaring, coming closer and closer.

And if I want to share the story of it, I'll tell you the old folk tale:

They say there once were two brothers, brother of the one on horseback,

Atop their steed when they passed this small hill. They both rode to an island Called Nags Head. To them belonged a Girl named Summerhill, and she had only one thing she needed to get well: her health to be sound like it Was five years before, when they fell And almost died together from typhoid fever. Then one of them asked him to make it last forever, or die trying. Now You might call me crazy, but… I Don't know what's happened to those two since they left… but it's definitely changed. for you, my friends—now that our summertime has ended. I don't care What the winter will bring when I am gone. You see, I'm not going 'til spring-summer next Year. So here I stand still, like an iron stake stuck in the ice. But not so high: I've been waiting ten thousand years to come back here. It won't matter Even if I stay There as long as everyone else will. No matter how much you hate me.

Into the languor of Nature’s quiet heart, Into the launching of windy songs, I find my soul on this sylvan path, Each step a stanza in the ballad of her art. On the serpentine trail, above the limits of the lowlands, the wild beauty of a verse awaits, carven by time in a secret braille. Each rustling leaf, a syllable of the stories of the mountain streams, Running in rivulets, brimming in sunlight, Echoes of a past day fading and yet unfading. The silhouette of the mountains against a purple sky, A sonnet to the darkness and the stars, A place where the moon recites an eternal elegy, In an amphitheater of silent joy. In the choir of the larks, in the meadows of wildflowers, In the songs of green, gold, and sunflower heads, I hear the hillside melody, A romance that expands and recedes. The wild peaks in the darkening west, The final lines of this holy quest, Where the poet’s heart, like a happy pilgrim, Finds a rimed haven, a tranquil rest. Every stone, every peak, is a stanza, Every mountain an eclogue, a sublime song, The romantic wanderer, lost in wonder, Drunk on the sound of the mountains’ timeless bells. And so I walk and listen to the soft mountain tale, Inscribed in the peace of the dale, My feet write my verses, I inscribe my verses, In this vast and pale poetry of life.

By Ellen Batista
I sit in the quiet of my home
Reading names in a book,
Smiling as I watch you grow,
Feeling your mother's love in my heart,
Knowing you are warm and safe,
I smile as I turn each page,
Thinking of you hunting births.

As I hunt with you, I find
Each moment of your life most rare,
For you are a special part
Of everything that I cherish most,
Each hopeful smile that you give,
Is a glimpse of your delicate soul,
Your gentle spirit it does enfold,
Within my heart it does mold.

You are the precious child of my friend,
A gift of love from above,
You are the innocent of our world,
With your whole life still to unfold,
As you hunt each birth with glee,
I will be there to watch you grow,
To share in your wondrous joy,
And as you hunt each eager birth,

Apathetic dawns and moody nights,

From voices that I cannot hear.
Guiding me through shifting lands,
Where seasons blend into one's hands.

Free from chains that bind my soul to places.
Unshackled by the weight of time,
I move with grace, without a rhyme.

As suns and moons share stories untold.
Creatures strange and wondrous throng,
The paths that I am led along.

I discover strange, familiar verses.

Memories hidden deep inside,
Awaken, as if from a long, wide stride.
Remembered moments, shyly peeking,
Reveal truths that were worth seeking.

In this sojourn through the unknown,
I find the threads that weave my home.
For though the path is hard to trace,

Seest thou not yonder tiny  creatures

See   how these ants for  their provision
Doe sweat and labour  both  in sun and shower
And with  their yearely, sore  encounter
Provide against the winter aery
And  sad  enduring famine's rage?

by John Keats (23 October 1795–23 February 1821)

A soldier, who long watch'd where England lay,  
Struck with a sudden thought began to say:—  
'As I have watched the ships come each day  
And borne the brunt of the battle's rage,  
There is one spot of English ground  
To which my footsteps yet turn with pride;  
For there at least my country shall be free,  
From the foul stain of slavery. O, could I there  
For once behold yon taper'd steeple rise,  
Or even from yon green hill's highest crown,  
But catch one glimpse of all that lies below,  
The woodlands, hills, and dales I could not know.'  
Thus having said the warrior stopp'd his ear,  
And at each pause kept time with his spear.  
Anon, with a smile at his lips he said:  
'Here are not wanting those who will dare  
All deeds of valour; but for me  
'Twould please me now, if I had one to lead  
From this wild camp through all the world,  
A life of soft repose:  
To pass in the low vale of Tempe by,  
And hear the nightingale sing in the rushes,  
By the river-side.  
To hear the brook run over the pebbles  
With many a sound that the hills re-echo,  
All round me, then to lie  
In flowery meads under the willow-tree;  
To gaze upon the stars and listen the breeze,  
And hear it murmur in many a reed,  
And see the river-brim  
Sail round the alders with shadows so dim,  
And dream of home through the day and night.'

Shall I waste in despair,
My days upon this earth,
In endless sorrow and despair,
My heart forever wrung?

Shall I give up all hope,
And let my spirit fall,
Into the depths of darkness,
Where none can reach or call?

Nay, let me rise and strive,
With all my strength and might,
To find the light that guides me,
And banish all the night.

For though the road may be,
Long, hard, and full of pain,
I'll not be overcome,
But press on to the gain.

So let me not waste away,
In idle grief and fear,
But face each trial as it comes,
And strive to do my best.

For in the end, I know,
That I shall rise above,
And find a peace that passes,
All earthly strife and love.

It was the morning of May 23, 2003, and I felt like I had been to the top of that mountain and seen a light I had never seen before. In the distance, over the green, craggy mountains of Switzerland, I could see the city of Geneva.

The only road in sight was a hilly, narrow dirt track through scrub forest. From up above, the light streaming through that narrow window was no different than the light of the setting sun. But from this spot, I knew I was standing over a continent, and as I looked down on that continent I saw it as if I were walking across the ocean. The mountains were just as flat and white, and the forest was just as green as the grass of the morning.

Then I remembered something else. "The New World" is an old poem, and I knew the last line of that old poem had to follow the last line of this newest one. The new one is the "New World." I walked that new continent and I saw it again and again and again. Over and over again it started anew.

As I walked that last mile over that last country rock I fell to my knees and held my breath until I couldn't breathe any more.

I stood and looked out at this new continent, where the tall pine, the huge fir and those black willow trees had stood, for hundreds and hundreds of years, and hundreds and hundreds of miles above me they had lit up that dark green planet with their brilliant, golden radiance. In the distance, over the mountains of Switzerland, the city of Geneva was rising, and I knew this new continent had been born from the blood of its inhabitants.

Through the windows of my bus in Geneva, the people of the New World looked at me. They held their breath and they walked on.

and yet wolf howls at moon

and the goat bleats as if in tune

I stand here in the nothingness of it all

as universe spits me out

or maybe I spit the universe out

I don't really know anymore

this is mystery which has no answer

as there isn't a god

that will ever ask question

for as I hear the beat

of those goats

I know that I have to get out of here

the wolves are howling now

took me a good long while

but here I am on goat path

and I can hear those damn wolves

getting closer to me

Soft snow blankets the ground,
In the quiet of early morn,
With determined steps and keen eyes,
The young boy sets out for the hunt.

He treads through the white, untouched terrain,
His breath crystallizing in the air,
With a determined glint in his eye,
He searches for signs of the furry prey.

He pauses, senses heightened,
A flicker of movement in the brush,
With a steady aim and a silent prayer,
He readies his rifle, and pulls the trigger with care.

The rabbit bounds away, a blur of white,
Vanishing into the dense wood,
The boy pursues with a determined chase,
His heart pounding with excitement and exertion.

He follows the trail, tracking the prey,
A glimpse of fur, and he's on the move,
Through thickets and over fallen logs,
He pushes on, undeterred by the cold.

At last, he spots his quarry,
Cauhgt in the open, frozen in fear,
With one final breath, he takes aim,
And pulls the trigger with precision and grace.

The rabbit falls, a soft thud on the snow,
Its life extinguished, but its spirit free,
The boy reflects on the journey,
A hunt well-fought, a lesson learned, and a memory to be.

In shadowy corners, dark deeds are done,
Where sinister plans are spun, and wickedness is spawned.
The evil that men do, it festers and grows,
A cancer that eats away at the soul, it shows.

With each step taken, a path is chose,
A journey downward, to dark place, it goes.
The innocent suffer, weak are preyed,
As cruelty and malice, are spread and swayed.

The cries of victims, they echo through time,
A haunting reminder, of evil that's done.
Their scars will never heal, their pain will never fade,
A constant reminder, of price they've paid.

But still, wicked, they walk among,
With smiling faces, and hearts made of stone.
They hide their true selves, behind a mask,
And laugh as they revel, in their wickedness and their task.

Yet, there is hope, a glimmer of light,
A chance for redemption, chance to make things right.
For those who seek it, who seek to change,
To leave behind, the evil that they've arranged.

But for those who refuse, who persist in their ways,
Their fate is sealed, their evil will stay.
Their legacy will be, stain on the earth,
A reminder of the evil that they gave birth.

So let us stand, against evil that's done,
Let us fight for justice, for love to be won.
For in the end, it's our choices that we make,
That will determine, the path that we take.

They dance upon their leashes, tethered angels,
Unaware of the world beyond their noses,
As human hands lead them through cities and alleys,
Guiding them to places unfathomable to their innocent eyes.

These gentle giants, descended from celestial beings,
Bestow their love through wagging tails and drooling smiles,
Reminding us of the purity we once knew
Before the darkness of the world besmirched our souls.

Yet, in their simple dog-mindedness,
They do not ponder their divine ancestry;
For them, there is only the joy of the moment,
Chasing squirrels and rolling in fragrant grass.

Oh, angel food dogs, how you elevate our spirits,
Lifting us from the mire of daily strife
With a simple lick or a warm, furry embrace,
Showing us, in your unsullied hearts, the true meaning of love.

Τhе sun sеts оn thе hоrіzоn,
Аs twо rіvеrs flоw іn sоrrоw,
Τhеіr wаtеrs dаrk аnd murkу,
А rеflесtіоn оf thеіr sоrrоw.

Τhе fіrst rіvеr tеаrs араrt,
А fаmіlу tоrn аsundеr,
Lоst lоvе аnd brоkеn hеаrts,
Τhеіr sоrrоw есhоеs lіkе thundеr.

Тhе sесоnd rіvеr flоws аlоnе,
Α frіеnd аbаndоnеd аnd fоrsаkеn,
Ιts wаtеrs сrу іn аgоnу,
Α sоrrоw thаt саnnоt bе shаkеn.

Τоgеthеr thеу flоw,
Ιn а rіvеr оf sоrrоw,
Тwо hеаrts thаt аrе brоkеn,
А lоvе thаt hаs gоnе аstrау.

Тhеіr wаtеrs blеnd аnd mеrgе,
А sоrrоw thаt nеvеr еnds,
Тwо rіvеrs fоrеvеr flоwіng,
Ιn а nеvеr-еndіng quеst fоr mеnds.

Тhе sun rіsеs оnсе аgаіn,
Вut thе sоrrоw rеmаіns,
Τwо rіvеrs flоwіng іn sоrrоw,
А соnstаnt rеmіndеr оf thе раіns.

The day was just beginning,
the sun shone bright in the sky,
I got into my car,
my favorite song playing on the radio. 
There was a flash of light, 
a blinding glare, 
I heard a voice speak, 
"You have run your car into me." 
Was it a hallucination, 
a trick of the light? 
No, it was God, 
standing there, 
in the middle of the road.

City of fireflies, a city of light, of luminous islands in space, but how bright! If one stood at a street corner and looked up, it was as bright as day. But no one looks up any more. Instead, each one walks ahead, face to the ground. A few carry a lantern strapped to their belt, instead of the candles or lamps of old, when they go out to look for a job that will pay less than what they have been getting; their supplies of food are dwindling, because no one is buying as much; their clothes are a rag every week, but they still have to pay the rent. What else do they do all day long? They haven’t noticed how hard life has been lately, but where they’ll be in another year, if things continue as they are, is anyone’s guess.

It's not often we speak openly about our pain or even our triumphs. Even this blog can be hard sometimes because I don't enjoy writing out my emotions like how I do here on my laptop because others see what I do through social Media so sometimes I have to censor Myself, especially when I write poetry because some people take their feelings VERY personally regardless if they ask me or not. I get why though...but at a certain point, self-care becomes necessary whether we want folks around us to understand Or not. I am sure Juanita herself wrote such an amazing piece because of everything she went thru...Everything WE go thru together. But Before someone Else understands I must first remember (And then Share) all these different parts with me…all sides of me and then some so I may eventually become who I am supposed to be even when I am Faced head-on into life's greatest opposition that'll test every part Of you mentally until one day where finally YOU realize that no matter how many times other people try their best against you; even after losing all those battles within yourself –you still made out stronger and better than ever Despite any odds thrown Up against us again.

Oh, my precious little girl,
With your eyes so bright and blue,
You fill my heart with joy and love,
And I am so proud of you.

From the moment you were born,
I knew my life had changed,
You brought a new meaning,
And my world was rearranged.

Your tiny fingers and tiny toes,
Are a miracle to behold,
You've captured my heart completely,
With a love that will never grow old.

I'll protect you from the world,
And shield you from any harm,
I'll be there to guide you,
With every step and every charm.

You'll grow up so quickly,
And become a woman strong and wise,
But always remember, my darling,
You'll forever be my prize.

So, sleep tight, my little angel,
Dream of all the wonders in store,
Know that you are loved beyond measure,
Forever and evermore.

A place of refuge, a place of peace
Where love and laughter never cease
A sanctuary from the world outside
Where hearts are mended, souls revived

With walls that hold a thousand tales
And floors that bear the weight of fails
It stands as testament to time
A symbol of enduring rhyme

In every room, a memory lies
A snapshot of life's surprise
From laughter-filled holiday feasts
To quiet moments, when hopes and dreams are released

Here, generations have grown and thrived
Their stories etched into its fabric, alive
In every creaky floorboard and beam
Lies the history of a family's dream

This house has seen it all, through the years
Joys and sorrows, laughter and tears
Yet still it stands, strong and true
A beacon of hope, shining bright and new

For in this house, we find our roots
Our sense of belonging, our cultural shoes
It's where our families come together
Where bonds are forged, forever tether

So let us cherish this sacred space
This refuge from the world's embrace
For here, we find our sense of home
In the fathers house, where love is sown.

In the depths of ocean, force so grand,
A current of water, a sight to behold,
Its power and strength, sight to command,
A force of nature, story untold.

From the shores of coast, it flows with might,
A river of water, force so pure,
Its power and strength, a wondrous sight,
A force of nature, a story so lure.

It flows through valleys, it flows through plains,
A river of water, a force so free,
Its power and strength, wondrous refrain,
A force of nature, story so sweet.

It flows through the mountains, it flows through land,
A river of water, a force so divine,
Its power and strength, wondrous command,
A force of nature, a story so fine.

The great grey water, a force so grand,
A river of water, a story untold,
Its power and strength, a wondrous command,
A force of nature, a story so bold.

Dusty roads bleed under a sullen sun,
A decade sighs, cringed under the economic run.
Whipped by winds, whipped by fears,
A timeworn fabric of dreams disappears.

Windows, once proud, dipped in despair,
Cracked mirrors reflecting a deepening scare.
On silent tracks, no steely beast roams,
Factories form fossils, desolate homes.

Crops lay dormant in barren fields,
Mother Nature shunned, no fruit she yields.
Prairies mourn, rivers dry, trees stripped bare,
Solitude echoes through the desolate air.

Men in tailored shadows, ghost towns abide,
Seeking solace under a penniless pride.
Empty pots and vacant eyes,
The depression speaks in weary sighs.

From the street corners, children peep,
Hunger etched onto their faces deep,
In soup-kitchen queues, they shuffle with hope,
Unaware of the impending economic slope.

Women in rags, their beauty faded,
With their strength, cherished dreams heavily traded.
The walls of security slowly crumble,
In the face of devastation, briefly humble.

An empty canvas of once bustling streets,
Rehearses the rhythm of defeat's beats.
Forgotten symphoney of laughter and joy,
Replaced by a grim silence, childhood toys.

In obsidian hearts, fires ignite,
Echoing resilience in the freezing night.
From resilient seeds, rooted strong and deep,
Emerges the spirit of dreams to keep.

Despite the lingering melancholy twang,
Despite the pain, the crushing pang,
Bravely striving against the cruel blow,
Life pushes forth, demanding to grow.

Thus wraps the tale of the Depression's frown,
A decade dressed in shadow's gown.
But within the heart of such woe and strife,
Lurked the invincible pulse of life.

I remember mama, her eyes so warm and tender,
A smile that could light up darkest room,
Her touch, so gentle and her voice so calm,
I still feel her embrace within my dreams.

She cooked the best meals, and her love was endless,
Her laugh, heartwarming and infectious,
In her eyes I saw reflection of my endless potential,
My heart, she filled with her unwavering support.

I remember mama, the way she washed my clothes,
The way she'd sing songs while she worked,
Her prayers at night, before I closed my eyes,
I still hear her voice, soothing my worries.

Life without mama isn't easy,
But her memories fill my heart with ease,
Though she's not physically here, she remains in my soul,
Her love, her wisdom, and her grace.

Mama, I remember you, and I will always,
Your love and memory, eternal,
You may be gone, but you'll never be forgotten,
Your legacy remains in my heart and in my emotion.

Convincing faith is not in words that we speak,
But in the silence of the heart that believes;
It's not in grand displays of piety,
But in the quiet moments we feel His love. Convincing faith is the gentle whisper heard,
In the stillness of the night, when all is bleak,
That whispers hope and promises salvation,
And fills our souls with warmth, dispelling all fear. 

Convincing faith is the strength that carries us,
Through trials, fears, and doubts, to see us through,
And though at times the path may be unseen,
Faith guides us on with an unwavering blues. 

Convincing faith is not an easy road,
But one that asks us to surrender our pride,
To lay our burdens down and seek the light,
And in His love, our souls will find a site. So let us have convincing faith that endures,
With hope that sees us through the darkest hours,
For in His love, we shall find the power,
To rise above, and conquer all our fears.

I was born in a small town,

My parents were poor and my father died when I was young.

He left me with his wife and two children.

They lived on their own for many years, but eventually they divorced.

When I was about ten years old, my mother remarried.

She had three more children by this time.

One day she told me that her husband had been killed in an accident.

Her new husband's name was John. He was a truck driver.

His death devastated my family. My mother never recovered from it.

After he died, my mother moved to another state.

She took all of our belongings and left us there.

We didn't know where we would go or what we would do.

It wasn't until I was twenty-one years old that I found out who my real father was.

John was a man named James.

James was a good man.

He loved his family very much.

But one night, while he was sleeping, he fell asleep and never woke up again.

That was the last time anyone saw him alive.

I don't remember how long ago that was.

I think it must have been sometime around the year 2000.

I've always wondered if my mother ever got over her grief.

Maybe she went back to live with her first husband.

Or maybe she stayed in California and raised some kids.

Whatever happened, I'm sure it hurt her deeply.

I wonder sometimes if she even knew that she lost her husband.

I hope so.

I wish I could tell her that I forgive her.

I wish I could tell her that I love her.

I wish I could tell her that I'll be here for her as long as she needs me.

I wish I could tell her that I will always be there for her.

I wish I could tell her that I am sorry.

In marketplace where commerce thrives,
A force of nature, the velocity of money arrives.
Like a river in constant motion,
It flows with purpose, creating commotion.

From hand to hand it quickly passes,
Empowering individuals, shattering classes.
Its speed a testament to its worth,
Sparking growth and revitalizing Earth.

As it trades goods and services with pace,
Economy flourishes, enhancing every space.
Investments made, ideas come to life,
New industries born, overcoming strife.

It moves through industries far and wide,
Fueling invention, with innovation as its guide.
Transforming lives and shaping destiny,
Powering progress, setting society free.

From the smallest transaction to global trade,
The velocity of money never fades.
It connects nations, transcending borders,
Breathing life into economies, creating orders.

But with its speed, a warning must be told,
For hoarding and hiding it within one's hold.
Like stagnant pond, it loses its might,
Leaving economies stagnant, causing a blight.

So let velocity of money roam,
Allowing it to find its rightful home.
In circulation, it holds true power,
Creating prosperity, hour after hour.

Let it flow, let it soar,
Unleashing potential that lies at its core.
For in its movement, we find the key,
To better future for you and me.

In the corner of the attic, wrapped in dust,
Lies a relic of a day, when love was just.
A silhouette of silk, a whisper of silk,
A memory of childhood, in a forgotten place.

Once beautiful as a poppy, blooming in the sky,
Now a muted echo of the wars won.
Threads of passion woven, in each seam,
Now a faded testament, of a forgotten dream.

She danced in you beneath the sun's warm light,
A crimson dance, in the world's grand show.
The rustle of your skirt, the sway of her shoulders,
The smell of sweet wine, on lovers' tongues.

You held her close, in the warmth of the dance,
In the throes of romance, in a timeless trance.
The echo of joy, the murmur of sighs,
The promise of tomorrow, in her youthful eyes.

Now you lie dormant, in the attic's darkness,
A ghost of the past, in a quiet tomb.
And outside your folds, the memories reside,
Of a woman in a white gown, dancing with joy.

The colour might have vanished, the cloth might have broken,
But the essence of her essence, in you is worn.
A symbol of her youth, her love, her zest,
Forever you remain, her faded blue gown.

When my mother died, I was very young,
Lost in the world, feeling utterly undone.
Her absence left me broken and alone,
A little chimney sweeper, with no place to call home.

The world turned cold, as I walked its weary streets,
With soot-covered clothes, no shoes on my feet.
I became invisible, a face in the crowd,
Enduring hardships that no child should be allowed.

Each day was a struggle, a constant fight,
To survive in a world that showed no light.
The chimneys I cleaned became my only shelter,
As I longed for a love that no longer sweltered.

But even in the midst of my darkest despair,
I held onto memories of my mother's care.
Her gentle touch, her comforting embrace,
Gave me strength and hope in this dreary place.

I would climb up tall chimneys, reaching for the sky,
Imagining my mother's spirit floating high.
She watched over me, guiding my uncertain path,
A guardian angel, in this aftermath.

I met others like me, swept up in this trade,
Bound by a fate that was cruelly made.
But amidst the darkness, we found solace in each other,
Sharing our stories and supporting one another.

Though we were trapped in a world so cold,
Our dreams remained vivid, unconsoled.
We longed for freedom, outside this chimney's grasp,
Searching for a brighter future, holding onto faith's clasp.

And as I grew older, still carrying my pain,
I vowed to break through this suffocating chain.
To rise above the soot, and reach for the light,
No longer a chimney sweeper, but with a spirit that ignites.

Years have now passed since that fateful day,
When my mother's love was taken away.
But her memory lives on, forever in my heart,
A guiding force that helped me make a fresh start.

I am no longer a chimney sweeper, lost and subdued,
But a survivor, who has overcome what he once knew.
With love as my compass, I found my way,
From the depths of sorrow, to a brighter day.

Once upon a time, in a world full of light, There lived a feeling which lightened the darkest night. The people called it happiness; A wonderful smile; And they knew not that it could not last long. The happy feeling pursued everyone, But a trace of joy was left behind it, Pure and bright, Pure and bright. Behind its face there was a deeper truth, A hidden frailty, a story rarely told. There is often a pleading for happiness, We always search for it, hoping it will return; But shadows are reflected in the blissful moments, As if happiness were a game no one could win. Like a butterfly, fleeting in the wind, Then it would go away, leaving us lonely. It is always elusive, a distant dream; Chasing happiness is a painful theme. Others would grab hold of it in fear, But the more they clung to it, the faster it would fly. It was the pursuit of happiness, that caused the most sorrow. Within the realm of happiness, there is a tragic theme; The theme of illusions, deceiving and chasing. It is true happiness that is paradoxical, Having the courage to face the heart’s agony. So let us not be misled by its enchanting radiance; Happiness is not always the best protection from grief. Hold it when it comes, know that it may go, As within our heart lies the story of happiness, A sad story of tragic love.

Весkеt rеfusеd tо bеnd оr соmрrоmіsе dеsріtе thrеаts frоm thоsе аbоvе hіm рlасеd,
Ηіs fаіth rеmаіnеd unwаvеrіng еvеn іf іt mеаnt lоsіng fаvоr wіthіn rоуаl grасе. 

"Whо wіll rіd mе оf thіs turbulеnt рrіеst?" сrіеd оut kіng untо hіs соurtіеrs bоld,
Αnd fоur knіghts rоdе fоrth tоwаrds Саntеrburу lаnd bеlіеvіng thеіr саusе just аnd оld. 
Тhеу еntеrеd thе саthеdrаl wіthоut fеаr thоugh dеер dоwn fеlt sоmе unеаsе, реrhарs sеnsіng dооm аhеаd,

Τhеіr swоrds ріеrсеd thrоugh flеsh аnd bоnе саusіng blооd tо sріll оntо mаrblе flооr bеlоw,

Сrіеs есhоеd thrоughоut hоlу рlасе аs реорlе sсrаmblеd tо еsсаре sсеnе оf hоrrоr shоwn,

Αn еtеrnаl rеmіndеr еtсhеd thеrе fоrеvеrmоrе аbоut соnsеquеnсеs bоrnе bу dіvіnе dіsоbеіsаnсе. 
Тhоmаs' lаst wоrds whіsреrеd sоftlу bеfоrе lіfе flеd аwау bеnеаth сrіmsоn tіdе:

Кіng lаtеr rеgrеttеd оrdеr раssеd whісh lеd dіrесtlу hеrе tоdау, rеаlіzіng tоо lаtе соst ехасtеd hеаvу tоll,

An Old Man's Winter Night

by William Wordsworth

I have been out upon the hills,

And made my way along the moorland track,

Watching the moon rise from the opposite hills,

And at her rising thus addressed the Night:

"O Night, if this be but a vain show,

Yet, in the train of thy departing grace,

Let my sad heart be stilled and reconciled

Unto the life that I have had to live." The Night was silent to my questionings,

And, being silent, in her silence she

Said more than could be put into words;

For she fulfilled my desire with me,

And to my heart did so much grace impart,

That, in her presence, all my being seemed

To be at peace, as is a weary man

That, having suffered long and been forlorn,

Sleeps suddenly and takes no heed for things,

But, in a happy dream, is brought again

Unto the days of his youth, ere sorrows were born. And, as I thus was carried back by thought

Unto the time when I was happy-hearted,

I seemed to see, as in a map, the course

Of all my life, traced out in loneliness,

A track circuitous, an upward track,

With many a winding, many a toilsome climb,

And many a steep and rugged declivity,

And many a dark and narrow defile,

Through which the torrents roared, and thunder-claps

Were heard, and lightnings flashed, and tempests raved. 

And, as I looked, methought I saw the track

Grow broader in the distance, and the way

More open and more smooth, and, as I looked,

The prospect brightened more and more, and, lo! 

The way was lost in sunshine, and the track

Became a smooth, straight, golden pathway, such

As leads a pilgrim to the heavenly city. And, as I looked, methought I saw the track

Grow broader in the distance

In hues of color, a story unfolds
A canvas alive, with secrets it holds
Strokes of brush, a symphony sings
A work of art, the artist's soul clings

With every glance, a message takes flight
A wordless tale, that touches the heart's light
A kaleidoscope of emotion in sight
A journey through hues, a feeling ignites

In this work of art, a piece of the soul
A glimpse of life, the artist's goal
A fragment of dreams, a shard of hope
A splendor of beauty, a world to cope

The colors blend, the lines converge
A symphony of form, an image emerges
A snapshot of life, a moment in time
A masterpiece born, a work of art divine

A reflection of passion, of love and of fire
A creation that beckons, a desire to inspire
A work of art, a treasure to behold
A symphony of color, a poem to unfold.

In the shadow of the Great Crash, despair reigns
A world falters, hope in tatters, the future in pain
The once beautiful streets now lonely, the silence a shroud
As people gather, fears unspoken, the darkness allowed

Breadlines stretch on, a never-ending plight
Hollow eyes, empty bellies, a desperate struggle
For scraps and crumbs, a meager share
A daily battle, with no respite, no care

The shantytowns rise, a bitter testament
To a dream that's failed, a world's disappointment
Tattered tents, a makeshift home
A bitter reminder, a generation's doom

The orchards lie fallow, the fields untended
A land that once existed, now forgotten
The farms wither, the livestock dwindle
A agricultural wasteland, a world's rustle

The workers stand idle, the machines still
A landscape of misery, a country's ill
The factories scattered, their skills forgotten
A generation's sweat, a future deplored

But now we dream, a hope of hope
A spark of strength, a people's scope
To rise again, to face the dawn
To build and mend, a new chapter to be drawn

For in the dark, a light flickers
A promise of change, a people's tickers
A pulse of life, a spirit that won't abate
A determination to overcome the weight.

With eager feet, she steps onto the ground
Her backpack full, her spirit sound
Excitement fills the summer air
As she leaves her parents' care

She boards the bus with friends by her side
A journey ahead, adventures to abide
The trees pass by in a blur of green
As they make their way to camp serene

The days will be filled with laughter and play
Crafts and games, new skills to sway
From archery to swimming in the lake
Her fears she'll face, her courage take

Nights spent 'neath the starry sky
Songs and stories, tears and sighs
In this place, she'll find her voice
And learn to embrace her choice

With memories made, lessons learned
New friendships that will forever burn
She'll return home, a different girl
Her heart full, her spirit unfurl

Ηоw slоwlу mоmеnts wіngеd thеіr wау аlоng!
Ηоw drеаrу rоllеd thе wіntеr's snоw-

Іn thе dерths оf оur hеаrts, а flаmе burns brіght,
А раssіоn thаt drіvеs us tо sееk thе lіght,
Τо bе sееn аnd hеаrd, tо mаkе оur mаrk,
То lеаvе а lеgасу thаt wіll nеvеr dаrk.

Іt's thе lоvе оf fаmе, thе unіvеrsаl раssіоn,
Тhаt fuеls оur drеаms аnd kеерs us іn mоtіоn,
То strіvе fоr grеаtnеss, tо rеасh fоr thе stаrs,
Τо lеаvе оur mаrk оn thіs wоrld, nо mаttеr hоw fаr.

Ιt's thе thrіll оf thе sроtlіght, thе rush оf аdrеnаlіnе,
Τhе fееlіng оf bеіng аlіvе, lіkе а nеvеr-еndіng lіnе,
Οf fаmе аnd fоrtunе, оf suссеss аnd glоrу,
Ιt's а fееlіng thаt wе саn't dеnу, nо mаttеr hоw hаrd wе trу.

Ιt's thе dеsіrе tо bе rеmеmbеrеd, tо bе іmmоrtаlіzеd,
То hаvе оur nаmеs еtсhеd іn hіstоrу, tо bе rесоgnіzеd,
Τо bе сеlеbrаtеd fоr оur асhіеvеmеnts, tо bе hеld іn hіgh еstееm,
Τо bе thе еnvу оf аll, tо bе thе tаlk оf thе tоwn, thе drеаm.

Sо lеt us еmbrасе thіs раssіоn, thіs lоvе оf fаmе,
Lеt іt guіdе us оn оur jоurnеу, lеt іt bе оur аіm,
Fоr іt's thе unіvеrsаl раssіоn thаt unіtеs us аll,
Аnd іt's thе flаmе thаt wіll lіght оur wау, nоw аnd fоrеvеrmоrе.
